reason: The text explicitly demonstrates that agency extends beyond leaders. While Moses is mentioned as a leader, the text states that 'Moses and the children of Israel' (בְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל) sang the song together, showing that non-leadership people collectively performed this action. Additionally, the text describes agency exercised by various peoples who 'heard and trembled' (שָׁמְע֥וּ עַמִּ֖ים יִרְגָּז֑וּן), and even the enemy is portrayed as contemplating action ('I will pursue, I will overtake'). God's agency is also central throughout the narrative. The composition and performance of this song is explicitly a collective action shared by leadership and non-leadership Israelites alike, contradicting the claim that only leaders have agency.
